title: The Real Reason Developers Burn Out on Web3
content:
It's not the tech. It's not the complexity. It's the fact that everything breaks in production and you only find out when users complain.

Traditional software has logs, monitoring, error tracking. Web3 has... block explorers and hoping someone screenshots the revert reason before the toast disappears. When a contract call fails, you are Sherlock Holmes with half the clues. Was it out of gas? Wrong network? A require statement? Did the user reject the signature?

The tools are getting better (Tenderly, OpenZeppelin Defender, custom error selectors), but the developer experience is still primitive compared to traditional stacks. You can't just console.log your way through a failing transaction.

What actually helps: simulate transactions before sending them, emit detailed events for every state change, and build debugging into your contracts from day one. The teams that survive are the ones that treat observability as a feature, not an afterthought.
